findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The reference doc is reached by a path in the working copy, which only exists when Athena runs on its own repository. The prompts that point to it are compiled in and used on every repository.
findings.evidence: README.md:8: Athena is for people who 'hand a repository a short request'. crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs:521-531 builds agent snapshots from a `user_repo`. The frames are compiled-in constants (include_str!), but docs/agent-reference.md would be an ordinary file in Athena's own tree. On any other repository the reader, planner, critic, producer and verifier would be told to read a file that is not there. The moved knowledge (forecast scoring, plan-field examples, verdict rules, severity scale) describes Athena itself, not the target repository. Athena already has a pattern for this: SYSTEM_FACTS is compiled in with include_str! (briefs.rs:1375) and delivered in the brief, and context-engineer.md §8 says briefs sit outside the budgets. The planned test `frames_name_the_reference_doc_and_it_exists` resolves the path from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, so it checks Athena's own tree and would pass while the pointer fails on every other repository. The plan's own rationale, 'all have Read over a copy that holds docs/', is true only for this repository. Fix: Deliver the reference without depending on the target repository. Options: (a) compile the doc in with include_str! and add each role's section to that role's brief, as SYSTEM_FACTS is, which keeps it out of the always-loaded sets (also update BUILD_PATHS and the CI cache key); or (b) have Athena write the compiled text to a fixed path in the agent's working copy, and test that path. If neither fits the scope, raise a User question to accept a pointer that only works on Athena's own repository, and say so in the doc and the CHANGELOG. Change the criterion-4 demonstration to exercise the delivery path an agent actually uses.
findings.location: Decision 2; Files: docs/agent-reference.md; Steps 3 and 7; Criterion 4 demonstration

findings.summary: The budget rule is a fixed +50 margin, not a principled headroom target, and it conflicts with the design's 95% displacement rule.
findings.evidence: docs/design/context-engineer.md:229-237 (§8): a change that leaves a set above 95% of its budget, or adds to one already above it, must name what it removes; Hestia flags any set above 90%. With the plan's targets, a producer set of about 927 tokens against a 950 budget is about 97.6%, and the verifier is similar. The new budgets would start above 95%, so the next small edit already needs an offset. The plan never mentions the rule. The rule is design prose only: Grep found no budget-guard or 90% flag in code. Fix: Derive the budget from a stated headroom target, for example the smallest multiple of 50 that leaves the largest set at or below 90%, while keeping contract + 2 verifier frames above the Verifier budget. Or state the choice against §8 in the lib.rs comment and the CHANGELOG.
findings.location: Decision 1 and Step 5 (round the measured largest set up to the next 50)

findings.summary: The plan leaves the stale budget figures and percentages in context-engineer.md in place.
findings.evidence: context-engineer.md:55, 141 and 232-233 quote 1300 budgets and percentages such as 'verifier 99.85%'. After this job they will be stale in a second way, because the budget itself changes, not just the size. No test reads them, as the plan says. Fix: Either update the figures in §8 and lines 55 and 141, or add one line to the CHANGELOG bullet noting they are historical.

summary: The plan reads the request correctly. It covers trimming the prompts, adding a reference doc and lowering the budgets. Its anchor list matches the wording tests I read in lib.rs:441-543. The dependents list is thorough: it includes run_pin_tests.rs:1607-1625 and system_facts_budgets_match_computed, and a Grep of .rs files for other readers of the 1300 values found only lib.rs and the synthetic fixture at briefs.rs:3598. The budget arithmetic also works. With the target sizes, contract plus two verifier frames (about 1110 tokens) stays above a verifier budget of about 950, so the test at run_pin_tests.rs:1618 still holds. One flaw is major. The prompts are compiled into the binary and used on any repository a user hands to Athena (README.md:8; the snapshot tests build a `user_repo`). The new pointer, `docs/agent-reference.md`, is a relative path in the working copy, so it only resolves when Athena works on its own repository. Everywhere else, the knowledge moved out of the prompts is simply gone. The new pointer test checks only Athena's own tree, so it passes even where the pointer would fail. A second, minor problem: the "round up to the next 50" budget rule is arbitrary. It puts the producer and verifier sets above the design's 95% line from the first day, and the plan never mentions that line.
